objective.value: Fine-tune the glycolytic flux ratio between the EMP pathway and the pentose phosphate pathway (PPP) in the previously constructed EP-bifido pathway in Escherichia coli to improve NADPH supply, carbon conversion rate and mevalonate (MVA) production, by (1) enhancing zwf expression via genomic promoter replacement and (2) dynamically down-regulating pfkA using a CRISPRi system.
objective.notes: The EP-bifido pathway itself (fxpk + fbp introduction, edd and pfkA knockout) was constructed in a previous study [13]; this paper optimizes it.

hypothesis.value: The detected EMP:PPP carbon split (0.43:0.57) deviates from the theoretical optimum (1:6), yielding insufficient NADPH; enhancing PPP flux by up-regulating zwf, and time-controlled repression of pfkA (whose knockout causes severe growth defects) via CRISPRi, will redirect flux, balance reducing power and improve MVA yield.
hypothesis.notes: Hypothesis grounded in prior 13C-MFA observation of suboptimal PPP split ratio and known growth defect of pfkA deletion.

(4) GFP reporter assay to characterize promoter strength.

NADPH level positively correlated with zwf promoter strength; main NADPH source shifted from TCA isocitrate dehydrogenase to PPP glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase; NADH total decreased; ATP total decreased but yield increased. CRISPRi: sgRNA1 (targeting pfkA promoter) best; strain BiB1F reached 8.53 g/L MVA and 68.7% conversion rate - claimed highest MVA conversion in shake-flask fermentation; CRISPRi strains showed inhibited growth/glucose consumption and almost no acetate/ethanol byproducts.

experimental_design_object.research_question: How to optimally and dynamically redistribute carbon flux between EMP and PPP in the EP-bifido E. coli system to maximize NADPH supply and MVA conversion yield from glucose.

experiments.outcome: BBa-J23100 strongest; J23100 and J23104 relatively strong; native zwf promoter weak (between J23108 and J23114); library-consistent

experiments.purpose: Enhance PPP flux and NADPH supply by replacing the genomic zwf promoter with graded-strength constitutive promoters, and test effect on MVA production
experiments.host: BW-P (BW25113 ΔpfkA::FRT) derivatives BW-P 23100/23104/23105/23108/23114-zwf, each carrying pBSA + pFF (BW-P10/04/05/08/14 BF)
experiments.intervention: genomic zwf promoter replacement via Red homologous recombination (CmR cassette, 300-500 bp homology arms); transformation with MVA pathway plasmids pBSA (atoB, mvaS, mvaA) and pFF (fbp, fxpk)
experiments.conditions: 50-mL shake flasks, M9 + 0.2% yeast extract + 20 g/L glucose, 37 °C, 120 rpm; MVA titers reported at 72 h (Methods state 48 h - inconsistency)
experiments.control: BW-P BF (BW-P/pBSA pFF, native zwf promoter)
experiments.readout: MVA titer and molar conversion rate (HPLC), OD600, glucose consumption over fermentation
experiments.analysis: comparison of titer/yield across promoter strengths; noted non-linear correlation between promoter strength and MVA yield
experiments.outcome: BW-P10 BF (J23100): 11.2 g/L MVA, 62.2% conversion at 72 h; BBa-J23100 and BBa-J23108 gave highest yields (64.3% and 62.3% mol/mol per Results text); growth and glucose consumption similar to control; fewer byproducts

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 passes (active promoter replacement on genome), Q2 passes (strains constructed in this study, Table 1 'This study'), Q3 passes (results demonstrate non-monotonic promoter-strength/yield relation, informing future fine-tuning choices).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Enhancing zwf (glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase) expression increases oxidative PPP flux specifically to boost NADPH supply - a reducing-power supply intervention (M2 前体与还原力供给).
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: Prior 13C-MFA of the EP-bifido MVA strain showed PPP split ratio too low (0.43:0.57 EMP:PPP vs theoretical optimum 1:6) with insufficient NADPH from oxidative PPP.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Trigger and outcome are measured: prior 13C-MFA split ratio, fermentation titers, and this study's 13C-MFA showing increased oxidative PPP flux and promoter-strength-correlated NADPH.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper explicitly states the mechanism: zwf is the first key PPP gene, its enhancement raises dehydrogenase flux and NADPH generation, and measured NADPH correlated with promoter strength; mechanistic link (stoichiometric NADPH generation by G6PDH) underlies the design.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When an acetyl-CoA-derived, NADPH-dependent product (e.g., mevalonate in an E. coli EP-bifido system) is limited by an EMP/PPP split skewed toward EMP, apply graded-strength promoter replacement at the zwf locus, because increasing G6PDH flux stoichiometrically raises NADPH supply - while noting yield does not scale monotonically with promoter strength, so a promoter ladder rather than the single strongest promoter should be screened.

experiments.purpose: Confirm that zwf enhancement redistributed flux from EMP to PPP and quantify cofactor (NADPH/NADH/ATP) generation changes
experiments.host: BW-P10 BF, BW-P08 BF; control BW-P BF; wild-type BW25113 as cofactor-derivation reference
experiments.intervention: none new - analysis of strains from EXP2 (13C labeling experiment)
experiments.conditions: 100% [1-13C]glucose 10 g/L, exponential-phase harvest, protein hydrolysis (6 M HCl, 120 °C, 24 h), TBDMS derivatization (105 °C, 1 h), GC-MS
experiments.readout: mass isotopomer distributions of proteinogenic amino acids; estimated flux map (Fig. 5); NADPH/NADH/ATP generation and derivation (Fig. 2)
experiments.analysis: 13C-Flux software minimizing residual sum of squares; isotope natural-abundance correction
experiments.outcome: Oxidative PPP flux increased, TCA flux decreased in zwf-enhanced strains; NADPH main source shifted from ICDH (TCA) to G6PDH (PPP); NADH decreased; ATP yield per glucose increased but total ATP decreased; TCA flux difference between BW-P10 BF and BW-P08 BF may explain growth differences

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 fails: 13C-MFA is a measurement verifying the EXP2 design, not a new engineering action.

experiments.purpose: Replace the static, growth-damaging pfkA knockout with time-controlled, tunable CRISPRi repression to dynamically balance EMP/PPP flux and improve MVA conversion
experiments.host: BW25113 23100-zwf (pfkA intact, zwf promoter replaced with BBa-J23100) carrying CRISPRi plasmid combinations: pBSA-dCas9+pFF-sgRNA1/2/3 (BiBF1-3) or pBSA-sgRNA1/2/3+pFF-dCas9 (BiB1F/BiB2F/BiB3F)
experiments.intervention: CRISPRi system: dcas9 under weak promoter BBa-J23134; three sgRNAs targeting pfkA promoter region (sgRNA1), +100 bp (sgRNA2) and +200 bp (sgRNA3) downstream of start codon; IPTG-inducible expression, induced with 200 µM IPTG at 12 h
experiments.conditions: same shake-flask fermentation regime as EXP2; induction at 12 h
experiments.control: BBF (BW25113 23100-zwf + pFF + pBSA, no CRISPRi); additional component controls BB1F, BBFd, BiBd1F (EXP5, Figure S1)
experiments.readout: MVA titer/yield (HPLC), OD600, glucose consumption, byproduct (acetate/ethanol) detection
experiments.analysis: comparison across three sgRNA target sites and vs controls
experiments.outcome: sgRNA1 (promoter-targeting) gave best repression balance; BiB1F reached 8.53 g/L MVA and 68.7% molar conversion - highest reported shake-flask MVA conversion; CRISPRi introduction reduced growth and glucose consumption (attributed to dCas9 toxicity/leaky expression); acetate/ethanol byproducts hardly detected

ddr_annotation.decision_type_rationale: Q1 passes (designed and built a tunable CRISPRi repression system targeting pfkA), Q2 passes (all CRISPRi strains constructed in this study), Q3 passes (comparison of three target sites yielded actionable finding that promoter-targeting sgRNA1 is optimal, informing future dynamic-regulation designs).
ddr_annotation.design_action_rationale: Time-controlled, inducible down-regulation of a competing-pathway node (pfkA) is dynamic regulation (M7 动态调控), replacing a permanent knockout.
ddr_annotation.trigger_observation: The static pfkA knockout in the EP-bifido strain caused severe growth defects, limiting applicability; early-growth carbon should ideally go to biomass, so flexible/timed repression was needed.
ddr_annotation.evidence_grading_rationale: Fermentation outcomes (growth, glucose, MVA titer/yield, byproducts) were measured for all six CRISPRi strains and four component controls.
ddr_annotation.reason_nature_rationale: Paper gives mechanistic reasoning: promoter-targeting sgRNA1 blocks RNA-polymerase binding via dCas9 steric hindrance while coding-region sgRNAs block elongation, yielding different repression ranges; growth-defect mechanism of pfkA loss is the stated trigger. Choice of weak promoter BBa-J23134 for dcas9 explicitly motivated by avoiding dCas9 toxicity.
ddr_annotation.generalizable_rule: When a competing-glycolytic-pathway knockout (e.g., pfkA) improves product yield but causes severe growth defects in an E. coli acetyl-CoA-derived production system, apply inducible CRISPRi repression targeting the gene's promoter region with a weakly expressed dCas9, because tunable, time-delayed transcriptional repression preserves early-growth EMP flux while still redirecting carbon toward the product pathway after induction.
alternatives_considered: Promoter-replacement methods for down-regulation (rejected: CRISPRi does not require genome editing of the target gene)
Post-transcriptional/post-translational tools such as anti-sense RNA and RNAi (mentioned as alternatives, not tested)

experimental_design_object.causal_dependencies: EXP1 (promoter characterization) informs promoter choice used in EXP2; EXP2 strains are subjects of EXP3 MFA; EXP2 result + prior growth-defect observation motivate EXP4 CRISPRi design; EXP5 controls decompose EXP4 effects.

extensions.engineering_paper_type_rationale: Core contribution is metabolic flux redistribution (zwf promoter engineering, pfkA down-regulation) for MVA production - metabolic_engineering. The CRISPRi dynamic/tunable regulation layer (inducible dCas9/sgRNA controlling EMP/PPP split) contributes a genetic-circuit/dynamic-control element, hence biosensor_platform as secondary classification (dynamic control circuitry, not a metabolite sensor).
